brief: 10 startup ideas hiding in plain sight in 2026 — what scrappy founders should build right now.

slots.stickyNote: here's exactly where I'd place my bets (and why)
slots.intro: I spent 2025 watching boring industries mint new millionaires. These are the gaps no one is filling yet.

slots.title: Sell shovels
slots.subtitle: AI regulation and retiring founders are creating instant demand.
slots.insight1Body: SOC-2 and EU AI Act docs are still manual for 50-person teams.
slots.insight2Title: Vertical AI voice agents for skilled trades
slots.insight2Body: HVAC and plumbing shops miss calls daily. Generic bots fail here.
slots.insight3Body: If a law forces spend, you have a budget line, not a nice-to-have.
slots.authorQuote: The best startups in 2026 won't be cool. They'll be necessary.

slots.title: Aging and
slots.subtitle: Boomers need care. Gen Z needs logistics. Founders need focus.
slots.insight1Body: Founders who built on FoxPro in '98 are retiring. Their data is trapped.
slots.insight2Body: TikTok shops need 2-day delivery without surrendering to Amazon.
slots.insight3Body: Aging parents and impulse buyers aren't trends. They're permanent shifts.
slots.authorQuote: I watch my friends and my parents. Both groups are desperate.

slots.title: Care and
slots.subtitle: The sandwich generation and construction crews share one pain: coordination.
slots.insight1Body: Adult children manage meds, bills, and aides via group chat chaos.
slots.insight2Body: Contractors wait 90 days for 10% holdback. Someone should finance it.
slots.insight3Title: Coordination pays more than content ever will
slots.insight3Body: Organizing messy human workflows beats another analytics dashboard.
slots.authorQuote: If it runs on WhatsApp and spreadsheets, productize it immediately.

slots.title: Touch the
slots.subtitle: Software-only is crowded. The edge now lives in warehouses and blood tests.
slots.insight1Body: Rent glasses + remote expert access to factories losing tribal knowledge.
slots.insight2Body: At-home finger prick → personalized groceries delivered Sunday night.
slots.insight3Title: AI is the interface, not the product
slots.insight3Body: Customers pay for outcomes. The model underneath is just plumbing.
slots.authorQuote: If it ships in a box or shows up in person, margins still exist.

slots.title: Commerce and
slots.subtitle: One fixes balance sheets. The other fixes remote work.
slots.insight1Body: Brick-and-mortar excess inventory is priced by gut feel. AI fixes that.
slots.insight2Body: Airbnb is too random. Companies need culture-designed offsite packages.
slots.insight3Body: A scrappy MVP in a boring market outruns a perfect app in a crowded one.
slots.authorQuote: I built my first company on a weekend. The idea was ugly. The revenue wasn't.

slots.title: Validate first
slots.subtitle: The founders winning in 2026 aren't smarter. They're faster at failing.
slots.insight1Body: If they won't pay for a spreadsheet, they won't pay for your app.
slots.insight2Title: Sell to the desperate, not the curious
slots.insight2Body: Curious buyers churn. Desperate buyers forgive bugs and pay upfront.
slots.insight3Title: Build for the operator, not the buyer
slots.insight3Body: The person doing the work has budget authority now. Bottom-up wins.
slots.authorQuote: My worst mistake was building for approvers instead of users.

slots.ctaBody: I write these essays at 2am because founders deserve honest maps, not hype. Which idea are you stealing?
